description: In accordance with FAR 5.101(c), this is a NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT. The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Office of Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and Human Capital Management Office (HCMO) intends to solicit and negotiate directly with Iron Mountain Information Management, LLC of 85 New Hampshire Avenue, Suite 150, Portsmouth, New Hampshire 03801-2926. DCSA requires shuttle bus services to include regular and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliant shuttle buses for DCSA employees at the Boyers, PA Iron Mountain facility. The Product Service Code (PSC) is V212 and the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 485991. The anticipated award date is December 30, 2026. The authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). Services may be deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued service of shuttle buses. Iron Mountain Information Management, LLC is the only known contractor who can provide the shuttle services at the Iron Mountain facility in Boyers, PA. The buses will provide service between the outside upper parking areas and work areas inside the facility during the designated hours of operation. DCSA is one of several tenants located on the Iron Mountain property in Boyers, PA. Iron Mountain exercises exclusive and comprehensive control over all access to the property including the roadways, parking areas, and internal transportation infrastructure used for the shuttle bus route. They are solely responsible for developing, implementing, and enforcing the security requirement for all lessors on the property. These requirements are extensive and necessitate a thorough vetting process for personnel and vehicles accessing the sites. While this notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes, interested parties may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide services identical to the shuttle services. This statement must include detailed technical documentation with specific evidence supporting the claim. Generalized marketing materials will not be considered. Submissions must be received via email no later than 9:00 AM EST on October 8, 2026. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred in the preparation of responses to this announcement. This is the only notice that will be issued for these services. A decision by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Definition of the requirement The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada (OSFI) has a requirement for a subscription to access curated Canadian macroeconomic data covering national, provincial, and regional economies, and Canadian Real Estate Association (CREA) data, delivered via an application program interface (API). The purpose of this Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is to signal the government's intention to award a contract for these services to Haver Analytics. Before awarding a contract, however, the government would like to provide other suppliers with the opportunity to demonstrate that they are capable of satisfying the requirements set out in this Notice, by submitting a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar day posting period. If other potential suppliers submit a statement of capabilities during the 15 calendar day posting period that meet the requirements set out in the ACAN, the government will proceed to a full tendering process on either the government's electronic tendering service or through traditional means, in order to award the contract. If no other supplier submits, on or before the closing date, a statement of capabilities meeting the requirements set out in the ACAN, a contract will be awarded to the pre-selected supplier. 3. Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: • Ability to Provide comprehensive Canadian macroeconomic and financial data covering, at a minimum, national accounts, employment and labour market statistics, inflation and interest rates, monetary and credit aggregates, government finance statistics, business and consumer activity indicators, population and demographic statistics, other major economic indicators required for economic forecasting and financial stability assessment. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and ongoing updates from official Canadian statistical agencies, central banks and other recognized sources. • Provide regional and sub-national economic data covering Canadian provinces, territories and major metropolitan covering, at a minimum, employment and labour market statistics, population and migration data, housing and construction indicators, income and consumption measures, prices and inflation indicators where available, regional economic activity and business indicators, and other regional economic indicators required for regional economic analysis and forecasting. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and ongoing updates from official Canadian statistical agencies, central banks and other recognized sources. • Provide Canadian residential real estate market information, including home sales activity, prices and price indices, housing inventory and listings, market supply and demand indicators, and other housing market indicators relevant to real estate analysis and financial system monitoring. Data shall include lengthy historical time series (50+ years where data exists) and be provided at varying levels including national, provincial and metropolitan areas. • Provide access to a software platform and/or web-based interface for searching, extracting, visualizing, transforming, and downloading data while maintaining data export functionality compatible with common analytical applications • Provide enterprise-wide license available for all OSFI users • Provide Documentation, training materials and user guides, as well as offer technical support, maintenance services, product updates and software enhancements (as applicable) • Provide programmatic access to subscribed datasets through a modern application programming interface (API) that supports automated retrieval of time-series data, metadata access and search functionality, bulk data extraction capabilities, standard authentication and security protocols, integration with statistical analytical and forecasting software, and machine-readable output formats such as JSON, CML, CSV or equivalent. 4. Applicability of the trade agreement(s) to the procurement This procurement is not subject to the following trade agreement(s) • Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) • Revised World Trade Organization - Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) • Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) • Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) • Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement (CUFTA) 5. Justification for the Pre-Selected Supplier Haver Analytics maintains exclusive ownership of curated macroeconomic and financial data products, including its user interface and analytical tools, proprietary data structures, series identifiers, concordance tables, historical vintages, and delivery formats. These elements are unique to Haver and are not reproduced or licensed through third party distributors. 6. Government Contracts Regulations Exception(s) The following exception to the Government Contracts Regulations is invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) - "only one person is capable of performing the work". 7. Ownership of Intellectual Property Ownership of any Foreground Intellectual Property arising out of the proposed contract will vest in the Contractor. 8. Period of the proposed contract or delivery date The proposed contract is for a period of one (1) year, with three (3) options to extend the contract for up to a period of one (1) year. 9. Cost estimate of the proposed contract The estimated value of the contract, including the option periods, is $46,559 USD 10. Name and address of the pre-identified supplier Haver Analytics 60 E 42nd St #3310 New York, NY 10165 United States 11. Suppliers' right to submit a statement of capabilities Suppliers who consider themselves fully qualified and available to meet the specified requirements may submit a statement of capabilities in writing to the Contracting Authority identified in this Notice on or before the closing date of this Notice. The statement of capabilities must clearly demonstrate how the supplier meets the advertised requirements. 12. Closing date for a submission of a statement of capabilities The closing date and time for acceptance of Statements of Capabilities is October 8, 2026 at 2:00 pm (EDT). 13. Inquiries and submission of statements of capabilities Inquiries and statements of capabilities are to be directed to: Cameron Marchand Senior Contracting Officer e-mail: contracting-approvisionnement@osfi-bsif.gc.ca 255 Albert St. 12th floor Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0H2

title: Specialized Vehicle Upfitting Services
description: Advance Contract Award Notice Definition of ACAN An Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is a public notice informing suppliers that Canada intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, and invites other suppliers to express their interest by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no other supplier submits a statement of capabilities demonstrating how they meet the set requirements in the ACAN by the closing date stated in the ACAN, the buyer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. Purpose of the ACAN The purpose of this Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) is to signal the Royal Canadian Mounted Police’s intention to award a contract for Specialized Vehicle Upfitting Services to Battleshield Industries Limited, as the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) believes this is the only supplier capable of providing all of the services within the National Capital Region, as set out in this Notice. Requirement description The Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Communication Security (COMSEC) has a requirement for Specialized Upfitting services for a vehicle, that will enable the RCMP to rapidly deploy a fully equipped mobile COMSEC Suite capable of processing high volumes of information efficiently. The work will involve the following tasks: 1. Planning, Design and Fabrication a. Create a layout plan (digital or sketch) for furniture, equipment, and wiring based on defined workspace needs including but not limited to desk space, storage, power, internet, seating, lighting, heating and cooling. b. Measure interior dimensions of the van. c. Check weight limits and payload capacity. d. Fabrication of a workable space for 2 to 3 users in the rear of the van, separate from the driving compartment of the vehicle 2. Electrical and Power Setup a. Install insulation and vapor barrier. b. Add wiring for outlets, lights, and devices. c. Install power system: d. Shore power connection e. Add LED lighting (ceiling, task, ambient). f. Mount Power outlets 3. Interior Build a. Install Flooring b. Build and install custom built in furniture c. Add seating solutions for workstations d. Add monitor and desktop mounts, including any necessary hardware for computer mounting e. Add wall panels f. Create compartment for network gear including but not limited to network switches, routers and cabling g. Custom cable run from workstations to network compartment 4. Mechanical and Safety a. Install heating and cooling b. Add climate control c. Include fire suppression system d. Installation of HVAC system CONSTRAINTS • All services must be executed at the Contractor’s secure facility. • The contractor must be located within the National Capital Region. Evaluation criteria for assessment of statement of capabilities (minimum essential requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate in their statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: • Maintains in-house engineering, design, fabrication, welding, electrical, and occupational health and safety capabilities at its facility, enabling performance of all phases of the vehicle fit-up project from design and fabrication through installation, testing, and final delivery. • Has successfully completed at least one (1) project within the last five (5) years involving the design and outfitting of a mobile vehicle, mobile command vehicle, specialty service vehicle, mobile workspace. • Possesses the capability to design and configure mobile operational workspaces, including the creation of scale layout plans that identify furniture location, storage, seating, electrical components and workstations. • Possesses the capability of installing vehicle insulation and vapor barrier systems suitable for year-round operation in -30 Degree Celsius conditions • Possesses the capability to design and install an integrated electrical distribution system, including wiring for outlets, lighting, and workspace equipment including but not limited to desk space, storage, power, internet, seating, lighting. • Demonstrates experience performing all the following services: integrating multiple vehicle systems, including electrical, HVAC, interior workspace, and safety systems into a single mobile operational platform. • Demonstrates experience delivering completed mobile operational or command vehicles for law enforcement, public safety, emergency management, military, or other government organizations. • Must be located no more than 50 Kilometres from the National Capital Region Trade agreement applicability This procurement is subject to the following trade agreement(s): Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) Justification for pre-identified supplier Battleshield Industries Limited has been identified as the proposed supplier because it possesses the specialized technical capabilities, secure facilities, and resources required to complete the conversion of a vehicle into a fully functional Mobile Operational Space (MOS) supporting RCMP COMSEC operations. The goal of this procurement is to increase operational readiness, reduce deployment times and reduce mobilisation costs for COMSEC’s mobile information processing. The project requires the in-house design, fabrication, integration, testing, and delivery of a customized mobile workspace incorporating electrical distribution, climate control, safety systems, custom furnishings, equipment mounting solutions, and vehicle-specific modifications. The work requires expertise across multiple disciplines and the ability to integrate these systems into a single operational platform. Battleshield Industries Limited maintains in-house engineering, design, fabrication, welding, electrical, and health and safety capabilities, enabling the company to complete all phases of the project from design through final delivery and testing. The company also possesses the specialized equipment and expertise required to manufacture custom components and modifications tailored to the vehicle and operational requirements. Battleshield has demonstrated experience designing and manufacturing specialized operational vehicles and mobile workspace solutions for Canadian law enforcement organizations, including projects involving complex vehicle integrations and customized operational environments. Market research conducted by the RCMP did not identify another supplier within the National Capital Region possessing the same combination of in-house vehicle integration, engineering, fabrication, electrical, and testing capabilities required to perform the full scope of work as a single-source solution. Due to the operational nature of the fitted vehicle, the RCMP requires the ability to obtain maintenance, repairs, warranty work, inspections, adjustments, and other post-installation support within a short timeframe to ensure continued operational readiness. A location within the prescribed distance from RCMP National Headquarters allows the vehicle to be transported to and from the Contractor's facility efficiently, minimizing vehicle downtime and the impact on operational availability. Exclusions and /or Limited tendering reasons The following exception(s) to the Government Contracts Regulations is (are) invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) - "only one person is capable of performing the work. Limited Tendering procedures as tracked under internal CAP Code 71 (iii), due to an absence of competition for technical reasons. This process is compliant with the following trade agreement provisions: CFTA Article 513(1)(b)(iii), CPTPP Article 15.10(1)(b)(iii), Canada-Chile FTA Article kbis-09(1)(b), Canada-Columbia FTA Article 1409 (1)(b)(iii), Canada-Honduras FTA Article 17.11(2)

description: Title: Economic Impacts of Rail Decarbonization in Canada Solicitation Number: 5000096225 GSIN: B101 UNSPSC: 77101500 Description: 1. Net-Zero Challenge Offerors of Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) are encouraged to join the Net-Zero Challenge. The Net Zero Challenge is a national initiative, led by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), that supports businesses in developing and implementing effective strategies and plans to reduce GHG emissions in facilities and operations to net-zero by 2050. The Net Zero Challenge aligns with Canada's obligations under the Paris Agreement to combat climate change and support Canada's Climate Competitiveness Strategy, which is building a prosperous net-zero future in which Canadian business and industry are well positioned to compete and lead in a global low-carbon economy. Currently, there is a mandatory federal requirement for high-dollar-value procurements. Moving forward, all offerors are encouraged to join the Net-Zero Challenge regardless of the dollar value of the procurement. Offerors who join the Net-Zero Challenge are encouraged to: a. Measure and disclose their greenhouse gas emissions; and b. Commit to planning, setting, and achieving science-based GHG reduction targets aligned with the objectives of the Paris Agreement. Participation in the Net-Zero Challenge not only supports global climate goals but also benefits businesses by positioning them as leaders in a global low-carbon economy. For more information on how to join, please consult the Net-Zero Challenge page. 3. Security There are no security requirements associated with this solicitation. 4. In performing the Contract and regardless of who acts as an importer, the Offeror must not, directly or indirectly, deliver Work if it is mined, manufactured, or produced wholly or in part by forced labour. 7. Check out Buy Canadian Policy for more information on what this could mean for you. 8. As such, offerors owned or led by Canadians from under-represented groups, such as women, LGBTQ2+ persons, persons with disabilities and persons from visible minorities, are encouraged to submit a bid for this opportunity. 9. Certification Requirements Contracts with former public servants (FPS) in receipt of a pension or a lump-sum payment must withstand the closest public scrutiny and reflect fairness in the spending of public funds. To comply with Treasury Board policies and directives on contracts with FPS, Offerors must provide the information detailed in the bid solicitation certification component. 10. Offerors should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. 11. Official Languages Environment and Climate Change Canada provides procurement services in both official languages. Offerors may submit a bid in the official language of their choice. 12. title: Nuclear Regulatory Framework Review – Writer
description: The objective is to engage the services of a writer, ideally someone with familiarity of Canada’s nuclear regulatory framework, to write and revise a number of discussion papers (likely between 5 and 7) and a What We Heard Report. The target audience for the documents is the public, as they will be published, requiring that the discussion papers and report be clear, concise, and capture the appropriate details. The discussion papers will be informed by Natural Resources Canada's (NRCan) initial engagement and policy development and will present potential options for changes to the nuclear regulatory framework to elicit feedback and suggestions through written submissions and engagement sessions. The What We Heard Report will summarize the feedback and suggestions received on the discussion papers, using material obtained from NRCan’s engagement activities. The writer will be required to attend videoconferences/meetings with NRCan officials for planning, organizing and feedback purposes.

title: Ft. Lee Obstacle Course Construction
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. Neither bids nor proposals are expected from contractors at this time. The actual solicitation is expected to be released approximately during the month of October 2026. The drawing and specification package will be included with the solicitation. Project Description: The purpose of this project is to construct a Confidence Obstacle Course (CFOC) and sheltered bleacher area with lightning protection. The CFOC will consist of twenty-four obstacle stations. Directional and obstacle signage will be provided to guide soldiers through the entire course. A 10ft maneuver trail between obstacles will be provided to support training or emergency vehicle movement through the course, to include the ability to bypass an obstacle on one side. A Tactical Assembly Area (TAA) of roughly half of an acre will be cleared in the center of the course and an entrance trail from TA-27 will be constructed. Gravel and fill dirt will be added to provide drainage away from the course and create a flat surface for all cleared areas. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 1-200-02) including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance.

title: Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline
description: ********************************************************************************** This amendment is to update the response date to 10:00 AM (AST) Thursday, 8 October 2026. ********************************************************************************** SOURCES SOUGHT - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FREEDOM CONNECTION NATURAL GAS PIPELINE THIS NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) OR INVITATION FOR BID. This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. This is not a solicitation for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this synopsis. No solicitation, specifications or drawings are available at this time. 1.0 Introduction and Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) is conducting market research for the construction of the Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline in Puerto Rico. The results of this market research will help determine the final procurement strategy. USACE-SAA is issuing this follow up Request for Information due to changes in the design, scope of work and acquisition strategy. This request is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of Small Business concerns, certified HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Businesses, Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business or Veteran-Owned Small Business. The responses or submissions will be used for informational and planning purposes only and do not constitute a commitment by the Government. The Government will not pay for any information submitted, and respondents will not be notified of the results. Submission or responses to this request for information is not a prerequisite for any potential future offerings. 2.0 Background The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is funding the Freedom Connection Project. The objective is to enhance the resilience of Puerto Rico�s northern power grid by improving fuel infrastructure. This project involves constructing an approximately 4.2-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline to supply the Palo Seco Power Plant from the existing San Juan liquid natural gas (LNG) terminal. SAA anticipates soliciting and awarding one (1) design-bid-build solicitation in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 15 and 36. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237120 - Oil and Gas Pipeline and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS code is US $45 million. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. Anticipated award date is in the second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Performance Period is 365 calendar days from NTP. 3.0 Scope of Work The scope of work includes all integrated procurement, labor, equipment, and services required to construct and commission the new pipeline based on a forthcoming final engineering design. Core responsibilities include: � Materials Procurement: Procure all necessary items, including long-lead items such as 20� steel pipe, valves, fittings, and instrumentation, ensuring compliance with the final design and industry standards. � Site Work: Prepare access roads and rights-of-way, and perform site clearing, grading, and stabilization. � Pipeline Installation: Execute all installation activities, including: Trenchless methods (e.g., Horizontal Directional Drilling - HDD). Open trench cut-and-cover installation. Pre-fabrication of materials. Pipeline welding, non-destructive testing (NDT), and inspection. Application of protective external coatings. Above-grade pipeline installation, potentially requiring more than 50 feet deep concrete piles. � Facilities Construction: Build all standalone facilities, including mainline block-valve stations and pig launcher/receiver stations, including electrical and instrumentation. � Delegated Design: Manage and execute any potentially delegated design elements (e.g., temporary works, trench shoring, specialized HDD drill profiles, or structural supports), including coordination with and sealing by licensed Professional Engineers. � Testing and Commissioning: Perform hydrostatic pressure testing, leak detection, and all pre-startup commissioning protocols. � Restoration and Handover: Restore all disturbed areas and formally transfer the completed pipeline and facilities to the owner/operator. 4.0 Requested Information for Capability Statement Interested firms must submit a capability statement (limited to 10 pages) that addresses the following. Responses should be tailored to demonstrate the firm's ability to successfully manage and execute this integrated procurement and construction project. Corporate Information & Experience 1. Company Profile: Provide your firm's name, address, point of contact (POC), CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 2. Business Category: Specify your firm's socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Business). 3. Bonding Capacity: Include documentation from your bonding company showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. 4. Project Experience: Interested construction firms may provide no more than three (3) example projects where the interested firm served as the prime contractor. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. Projects similar in scope to this project include: Natural gas pipeline project of similar magnitude and complexity where your firm was responsible for both materials� procurement and construction. Civil projects involving trenchless technologies like HDD, and work in dense urban or environmentally sensitive areas. Each project must comprise of detailed scope of the work, performance timeline, dollar value, customer name. Construction of pipelines of more than 1 mile in length including trenchless pipeline installation, including horizontal directional drilling, jack and bore, and other trenchless technologies. 5.0 Submission Instructions � Deadline: Responses must be submitted via email no later than 10:00 AM (AST), Tuesday, 24 September 2026. � Email To: Angel.J.Martinez@usace.army.mil and Meranda.R.Booth@usace.army.mil. � Format: No hardcopy or facsimile submissions will be accepted. description: 5P468-26-0177/A Interior redevelopment of the Arsenal Foundry – Québec Unit Field BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT The Arsenal Foundry, located near Saint-Jean Gate in Old Québec, is a red-brick industrial building constructed between 1902 and 1906. Owned by Parks Canada, it is currently used as a museum space and as a venue for various rental events. In the fall of 2026, the interior structures currently installed within the building will be demolished to restore the building’s original interior volume and allow the redeployment of heritage machinery and exhibits on a single level. The demolition work will create an interior opening providing access to a lower level containing a nineteenth-century masonry remnant. title: A&E IDIQ Sources Sought for Minnesota
description: SOURCES SOUGHT The purpose of this sources sought is to gain knowledge of potential sources including interested Small Business sources. This notice is for planning purposes only. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice or any follow up information requests. All interested parties should respond. The United States Property & Fiscal Office (USPFO), Minnesota National Guard, intends to solicit for Non-Personal Architect-Engineer (A-E) Services Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract for St. Paul, MN location in support of the 133rd Airlift Wing and Duluth, MN in support of the 148th Fighter Wing. Official solicitations will be posted in accordance with Public Law 92-582 (Selection of A-E Statute) and RFO Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 36. Selection of A-E firms will not be based upon competitive bidding procedures, but rather upon the professional qualifications necessary for the performance of the required services in accordance with RFO FAR 36. The AE firm must be capable of responding to and working on multiple task orders concurrently. As a result of this announcement, the Minnesota National Guard intends to award one Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for a period of five years to provide A-E services in support of Air National Guard (ANG) mission requirements located at the 133rd Airlift Wing, St. Paul, MN and Duluth, MN in support of the 148th Fighter Wing. These are not requirements contracts. All firms responding to this announcement are cautioned to review RFO FAR 9.5 - Organizational and Consultant Conflicts of interest; and RFO FAR 36.201-1(b). The Government contemplates awarding one (1) Single Award Task Order Contract, with a five (5) year ordering period. Firm Fixed Price Task Orders will be negotiated and awarded for each specific project. The total contract ceiling amount is anticipated to be $20 million for the life of the contract. Task orders will be primarily for projects with a construction value that typically result in an A-E task order less than $1,000,000.00 but maybe up to $5,000,000.00. Anticipated A-E services for MN ANG may include but are not be limited to performance of planning, master planning, and program support; A-E investigative and design services including development of construction documents; construction support; engineering and environmental studies, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) documentation; investigations and surveys in support of the Air National Guard Programs. Typical work may include, but is not specifically limited to: A: the preparation of plans, specifications, calculations, and cost estimates; B: the development of cost management, quality control and quality assurance plans; C: construction inspection, testing and management services; D: development of engineering standards; E: preparations for design submissions; F: technical, economic, planning, environmental, value engineering and other studies, analyses, surveys, investigations, and reports; G: development of performance criteria for bridging documents for design build projects; H: development of documents to support various government construction programs; I: commissioning services; J: comprehensive interior design. Services may also include, but are not limited to, a wide variety of professional services in support of projects for administrative, industrial, and support facilities to meet the needs of the Air National Guard. Various projects may include services associated with National Guard installations/facilities, such as aircraft hangars, Corrosion Control Facilities, aircraft maintenance facilities, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF), vehicle maintenance facilities, support equipment maintenance facilities, administrative offices, supply facilities, civil engineering facilities, training site facilities, security forces facilities, communications and electronic maintenance, mobility and aerial port facilities, dining facilities, medical training facilities, roadways, military airfield pavements, site utilities, infrastructure, and other support facilities. Additionally, task orders may be issued for support services which require A-E Services as defined in RFO FAR 2.101. THERE IS NO SYNOPSIS OR SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this sources sought is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your firm has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: All interested concerns will provide a response no later than 10:00 am (CDT) 08 October 2026. An electronic (email) response is the accepted method. This notification, shall not exceed five pages, must include: (1) Positive statement of intent to propose as a prime contractor. (2) Organization name, address, email address, website address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership (small business, Hubzone, large, etc.) for the organization. (4) A brief outline of resources, subcontractors, and key personnel that would be used to accomplish the contract. description: La Ley 19/2010, de 22 de diciembre, de Medidas Financieras y de Creación del Ente Público Instituto para la Competitividad Empresarial de Castilla y León (ICECYL), y el Decreto 67/2011, de 15 de diciembre, por el que se aprueba su Reglamento General atribuyen a ICECYL sus competencias de actuación. El Acuerdo del Consejo de Administración del ICECYL de fecha 3 de julio de 2023, por el que se aprueba su estructura organizativa, dispone la creación de la Secretaría General, como órgano centralizador de carácter transversal, que prestará funciones de apoyo y servicio interno a la propia entidad. La Secretaría General es responsable, entre otras cuestiones, de articular todas aquellas acciones relacionadas con la gestión de infraestructuras propias, incluidos aquellos asuntos de régimen interior que afectan a su funcionamiento diario, entre los que se encuentra la prestación de servicios de restauración para trabajadores y usuarios de las instalaciones propiedad del ICECYL. En el edificio del Centro de Soluciones Empresariales (CSE) de Arroyo de la Encomienda en la provincia de Valladolid, propiedad del ICECYL, se prestan servicios de cafetería y comedor tanto a los empleados públicos del propio ICECYL y del resto de entidades públicas ubicadas en el edificio CSE, como al público general que desean realizar trámites administrativos en dicho edificio. El ICECYL carece de medios propios para realizar este servicio, no teniendo personal especializado en restauración, por lo que resulta beneficiosa y conveniente la externalización de este servicio, lo que se pone de manifiesto a efectos de lo dispuesto en el artículo 116.4 de la Ley 9/2017, de 8 de noviembre, de Contratos del Sector Público (LCSP). Se considera que la concesión de servicios, a riesgo y ventura del contratista, es la solución más idónea para alcanzar los objetivos del contrato y responde a lo previsto en la LCSP. De conformidad con lo previsto en el artículo 289.1 de la LCSP, el adjudicatario será retribuido directamente por los usuarios de los servicios comprendidos en el objeto del contrato en función de la utilización de los mismos. Dada la naturaleza del presente contrato, sin presupuesto base de licitación, no procede tramitación presupuestaria. Por lo expuesto en los párrafos anteriores, en el presente contrato no hay precio entre las partes del mismo, ni procede tramitación presupuestaria.

title: Age-friendly Training
description: The Centre for Ageing Better is seeking a contractor to lead the research, design, and development of age-friendly training products that will support customer facing organisations be more age-friendly. The Age-friendly Training project aims to improve the quality and uptake of age-friendly training across the UK, helping more staff in customer-facing settings to have the understanding and motivation to make services more accessible and inclusive for older people. The successful bidder will lead a design process - understanding needs and co-producing training with those who may be implementing or receiving the final training. They will research the current age-friendly training landscape, identify what training products are needed for different audiences, and develop, test and refine training products that can be used by age-friendly communities and other organisations across diverse local contexts. The successful bidder will bring expertise in producing training products related to topics such as EDI, accessibility, health inequalities and service delivery. They will have a good understanding of the types of training approaches that are effective to enable learning and behaviour change of those working in customer-facing settings. title: FY 27 NRRE SETA Engineering Services
description: The Global Force Management (GFM)/Navy Readiness Reporting Enterprise (NRRE) program provides the authoritative systems used by the Navy to satisfy the requirements of the GFM Data Initiative (GFM-DI) and used unit and group Commanders to assess and report readiness. It provides the primary tools used to support the readiness decisions of commanders for operations and contingency planning at all levels of the Navy and Joint command structures. The GFM/NRRE program is the means by which the Navy complies with the readiness reporting requirements of the United States Code, Title 10. It provides critical support to the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), Combatant Commanders, CNO, and GFM decision processes. The GFM/NRRE is also the basis for reporting Navy readiness to the National Command Authority (NCA) and Congress. The principal GFM/NRRE systems process information determined to be vital to the operational readiness or mission effectiveness of deployed and contingency. Consequently, the loss of integrity or availability of the GFM/NRRE systems is unacceptable and could cause the immediate and could cause immediate and sustained loss of mission effectiveness. This is a service acquisition task to provide System Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) to GFM/NRRE Program Management Office (PMO) at U. S. Fleet Forces Command (USFF). The GFM/NRRE PMO requires highly specialized SETA services as defined in FAR 9.505-1 that include a combination of substantially all of the following activities: determining specifications, identifying and resolving interface problems, developing test requirements, evaluating test data, supervising design. These services also include providing technical direction through a combination of substantially all of the following activities: developing work statements, determining parameters, directing other contractors� operations, and resolving technical controversies. These services are required for the GFM/NRRE PMO to efficiently and effectively execute operations and sustainment, systems engineering, software design/development, integration, testing, evaluation, installation, training, life cycle maintenance, program management, and acquisition management of the GFM/NRRE Program of Record as the Chief of Naval Operations� Executive Agent.

title: FY 27 NRRE SETA Engineering Services
description: The Global Force Management (GFM)/Navy Readiness Reporting Enterprise (NRRE) program provides the authoritative systems used by the Navy to satisfy the requirements of the GFM Data Initiative (GFM-DI) and used unit and group Commanders to assess and report readiness. It provides the primary tools used to support the readiness decisions of commanders for operations and contingency planning at all levels of the Navy and Joint command structures. The GFM/NRRE program is the means by which the Navy complies with the readiness reporting requirements of the United States Code, Title 10. It provides critical support to the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), Combatant Commanders, CNO, and GFM decision processes. The GFM/NRRE is also the basis for reporting Navy readiness to the National Command Authority (NCA) and Congress. The principal GFM/NRRE systems process information determined to be vital to the operational readiness or mission effectiveness of deployed and contingency. Consequently, the loss of integrity or availability of the GFM/NRRE systems is unacceptable and could cause the immediate and could cause immediate and sustained loss of mission effectiveness. This is a service acquisition task to provide System Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) to GFM/NRRE Program Management Office (PMO) at U. S. Fleet Forces Command (USFF). The GFM/NRRE PMO requires highly specialized SETA services as defined in FAR 9.505-1 that include a combination of substantially all of the following activities: determining specifications, identifying and resolving interface problems, developing test requirements, evaluating test data, supervising design. These services also include providing technical direction through a combination of substantially all of the following activities: developing work statements, determining parameters, directing other contractors� operations, and resolving technical controversies. These services are required for the GFM/NRRE PMO to efficiently and effectively execute operations and sustainment, systems engineering, software design/development, integration, testing, evaluation, installation, training, life cycle maintenance, program management, and acquisition management of the GFM/NRRE Program of Record as the Chief of Naval Operations� Executive Agent.
